forms.title: Risk assessment
forms.description: Assesses the risks of providing care to this person, with a check of their home or room, before care begins or on admission and at each review.

fields.label: Purpose and scope
fields.hint: This assessment covers the risks of providing care and support to this person, and includes a check of their home (home care) or room (care homes), completed before care begins or on admission. Read it alongside our safeguarding, infection prevention and control and medicines policies, the person's care and support plan and PEEP, and, in care homes, the fire, legionella and environment risk assessments.

fields.label: Risk rating
fields.hint: Likelihood: 1 rare, 2 unlikely, 3 possible, 4 likely, 5 almost certain. Severity: 1 negligible, 2 minor, 3 moderate, 4 major, 5 catastrophic. Rating = likelihood × severity. 1–6 Low (routine monitoring); 7–14 Medium (action needed within a set timescale); 15–25 High (immediate action; consider whether the activity can safely continue until the risk is controlled).

fields.label: Risks to this person and to staff
fields.hint: For each area, record the risk and its rating. Choose Not applicable where an area does not apply.

fields.label: Moving and handling

fields.label: Falls
fields.hint: Including the bedroom and communal areas. Describe the risk, who might be harmed, likelihood (1–5) and severity (1–5), the control measures in place, and any further action needed (what, who, by when).

fields.label: Fire safety
fields.hint: General fire risks for this person. See their PEEP for evacuation planning, and the fire risk assessment in care homes. Describe the risk, who might be harmed, likelihood (1–5) and severity (1–5), the control measures in place, and any further action needed (what, who, by when).

fields.label: Infection prevention and control
fields.hint: Including care workers moving between households (home care) or a communal living environment (care homes). Describe the risk, who might be harmed, likelihood (1–5) and severity (1–5), the control measures in place, and any further action needed (what, who, by when).

forms.description: Our plain-language welcome guide for the people we support and their families, explaining what to expect, their rights and who to contact; reviewed yearly.

fields.label: Welcome
fields.hint: Write a warm, plain-language welcome introducing the service, its values, and what people and families can expect. Avoid jargon — this guide should be easy to read for the people we support and their families.

fields.label: About us
fields.hint: Describe who runs the service, how long it has been running, and its approach or philosophy of care.

fields.label: Starting with us
fields.hint: Describe what happens before and as care starts (or a resident moves in), including the pre-admission or initial assessment, care planning, and how people are supported to settle in.

fields.label: Before and as your care starts
What to bring / suggested belongings (care homes)
How your care plan is agreed with you
Your keyworker and who to ask for help
Your room (care homes)
fields.hint: Describe what is provided in each resident's room, options for personalising the space, and arrangements for looking after personal belongings.

fields.label: Meals and mealtimes
fields.hint: Describe mealtimes and menu choices (or the help we give with meals at home), how dietary and cultural preferences are catered for, and options for eating in your room or in communal dining areas.

fields.label: Daily life and activities
fields.hint: Describe the activities programme, outings, and how people can suggest activities they would enjoy.

fields.label: Personal care and support
fields.hint: Describe how personal care is provided, respecting dignity, privacy and individual preferences, e.g. choice of care worker gender where possible.

fields.label: Your health
fields.hint: Describe how healthcare needs are met, including GP visits, other health professionals involved, and how medicines are managed. Cross-reference the medicines management policy and consent policy in plain language.

fields.label: Visiting (care homes)
fields.hint: Describe visiting hours and arrangements, including for close family and friends, and any support available for residents who wish to go out.

fields.label: Keeping you safe
fields.hint: Explain, in plain language, how we keep people safe, including fire safety and what to do in an emergency, and how to raise a safeguarding concern.

fields.label: What to do if you feel unsafe or worried about your treatment
Who you can talk to in confidence
Your money and belongings
fields.hint: Describe arrangements for managing personal money and valuables, if we provide this support, and how this is recorded and safeguarded.

fields.label: Making a complaint
fields.hint: Explain simply how to raise a concern or complaint, referencing the complaints policy and procedure, and reassure people that raising a concern will not affect their care.

fields.label: Your consent and your rights
fields.hint: Explain in plain language that people will be asked for their consent before care is given, what happens if someone needs help to make decisions, and that people have the right to make their own choices wherever possible.

fields.label: Your information
fields.hint: Explain simply how personal information is kept private and only shared when necessary, and how a person can see their own care records.

fields.label: Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman
Your feedback
fields.hint: Invite people and families to give feedback at any time, and describe how feedback is used to improve the service.

forms.title: Staffing structure
forms.description: Sets out the home's organisational structure, staffing establishment, shift pattern, minimum staffing levels and reporting lines; reviewed yearly.

fields.label: Organisational structure overview
fields.hint: Describe the overall structure, e.g. lines of accountability from care staff through senior carers and the Deputy Manager to the Registered Manager, and from the Registered Manager to the Nominated Individual and Provider or Board.

fields.label: Staffing establishment
fields.hint: One line per role: role, reports to, establishment (FTE), current headcount, vacancies. Roles: Provider / Board, Nominated Individual, Registered Manager, Deputy Manager, Senior Care Assistant, Care Assistant, Activities Coordinator, Catering Lead / Chef, Kitchen Assistant, Housekeeping / Domestic Staff, Laundry Assistant, Maintenance / Facilities, Administrator.

fields.label: Shift pattern and minimum staffing levels
fields.hint: Describe the shift pattern used and the minimum safe staffing levels for each shift, based on current occupancy and dependency levels. Cross-reference the dependency tool used, if any, and the staff rota and attendance log.

fields.label: Early shift: senior or nurse cover
Late shift: senior or nurse cover
Night shift: senior or nurse cover
Adjusting staffing levels
fields.hint: How staffing levels are reviewed and adjusted in response to changes in occupancy, dependency or acuity, and the process for using bank or agency staff to cover gaps, cross-referencing the Recruitment Policy.

fields.label: Review
fields.hint: How often this document is reviewed and who is responsible, e.g. quarterly, or sooner after a significant change in occupancy or residents' needs.

fields.label: Comments on care planning and records
Call monitoring and punctuality
fields.hint: Some councils now require providers to submit call log data weekly through an online portal, rather than only checking it on a visit. This data is typically used to check punctuality, visit duration, and that visits are not scheduled back-to-back so tightly that a support worker cannot realistically get from one to the next (sometimes called "clustering" or "crammed" runs). Make sure rotas allow realistic travel time between visits, not just the care time itself.

Where the evidence is kept

forms.title: Care home inspection readiness
forms.description: A self-check against the questions councils and inspectors ask of care homes, section by section, with the evidence held and actions needed; completed ahead of an inspection or quality visit.

fields.label: Do you ensure care plans are person-centred, include the tasks people can do independently, and involve people in creating their care plan?
Do you link risk assessment information within all areas of the care plan, and are risks assessed in a timely manner?
Do you have a process for reviewing care plans and risk assessments, and for passing this information on to staff and other services / partners?
fields.hint: Note how the information is passed on.

fields.label: Can you evidence an audit process for the review of care plans and risk assessments?
Have you gained consent from people or the relevant person for the decision to live at the home, receive care, have photographs taken and have medication administered?
fields.hint: If consent is managed electronically, note how.

fields.label: Do you have individual PEEPs in place, and a system to review them?
Does the care plan reflect appropriate guidance from health and social care professionals?
Do you have a transfer of information process for hospital admissions and moves to other services (e.g. health action plan / hospital passport), and is it specific to each person?
Does your service complete daily logs for each person, showing who completed them, dates, times and comments?
Is the care plan signed by the resident or a relative / advocate?
fields.hint: If yes, note whether on paper or electronically.

fields.label: Does the care plan have a section / one-page profile of the resident's lifestyle, likes and preferences?
Can you evidence a deterioration tool is used?
Are residents' oral health care plans being followed and reviewed?
Can you evidence individual outcomes are met / achieved?
Can you evidence that staff handovers are in place and include each person's mood and wellbeing?
Evidence and actions
fields.hint: What evidence you hold for care plans and risk assessment, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: If a person lacks capacity, has family or advocacy support been considered?
Can you provide evidence of a schedule of DoLS status for individuals?
Can you evidence that conditions attached to the DoLS are being carried out?
Is the DoLS status for each individual evidenced in their care plan?
Is there evidence that DoLS authorisations are reapplied for 28 days before the existing DoLS expires?
Is decision-specific care supported by a best interest and MCA decision document, with a copy of the mental capacity assessment on file?
Are staff familiar with the local safeguarding process and aware of the local authority's provider concerns process / policy, and is this on display for staff?
Do staff have access to the whistleblowing policy?
Do you encourage staff to be proactive in relation to whistleblowing, and are they supported and protected?
fields.hint: Note how staff are supported and protected.

fields.label: Do you complete root cause analysis when investigating incidents?
Is there a record of staff training around safeguarding?
Have your staff attended MCA / DoLS training, and are they aware of the legislation?
Following a safeguarding alert, do you have a process to review and reflect on the outcomes and lessons learnt, and prevent further escalation to safeguarding?
fields.hint: If yes, note how this is measured and monitored.

fields.label: Does your service have a process for dealing with safeguarding, and is a copy easily accessible to staff?
Is feedback given to staff when they raise a safeguarding concern?
fields.hint: Note how feedback is given.

fields.label: Do you have a mechanism for learning from complaints, SARs, LeDeR reviews and coroner's inquests?
Are you aware when complaints may be escalated to safeguarding?
Do you have a safeguarding lead / officer for your service, and a deputy for when they are not available?
Evidence and actions
fields.hint: What evidence you hold for safeguarding, MCA and DoLS, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: End of life care and wishes
Can you evidence a current end of life training programme for staff supporting people who need end of life care?
Is your organisation actively seeking an end of life training programme?
Can you evidence documentation to support DNAR / ReSPECT or the equivalent local process and policy for each person?
Can you evidence that a new end of life care plan has replaced the existing care plan where required?
Do you have reflective processes, either individual or team?
Can you evidence last wishes and wills have been discussed with residents?
Do you have an end of life lead / officer within the organisation?
Evidence and actions
fields.hint: What evidence you hold for end of life care and wishes, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: Do you have a pressure ulcer management plan in place for anyone with a risk score of 10?
Can you evidence audits, monitoring, cleaning and maintenance of pressure-relief equipment?
Do you have a 24-hour contingency response for failing equipment?
Is there a process for reporting grade 3 pressure sores and above to safeguarding and CQC?
Do you have evidence of additional health professionals supporting the healing process?
Is there a skin integrity referral protocol, process and treatment plan in place?
Do you use a validated scale to support clinical judgement for all residents, from admission onwards, when assessing pressure ulcer risk?
Is there a process for staff to report skin integrity concerns, e.g. a red area or pressure wound?
Are body maps completed by staff when areas at risk are identified?
Evidence and actions
fields.hint: What evidence you hold for tissue viability, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: Do you have an up-to-date medicines policy and covert medicines policy, reviewed in the last 12 months?
Have you had an inspection by the medicines optimisation team in the last 12 months?
fields.hint: Note the date.

fields.label: Have you actioned the recommendations made?
Can you evidence that medication audits are undertaken and reviewed?
Are controlled drugs stored in a cabinet that meets legal requirements, with access restricted to authorised staff?
Are controlled drugs recorded in a separate bound register, with a separate page for each patient, drug, formulation and strength?
Is a stock check of controlled drugs carried out regularly?
fields.hint: At least weekly for homes with little controlled drug use; daily for homes with higher use.

fields.label: Are all medications, including thickeners, oxygen and sip feeds, stored securely in a locked room or cupboard as appropriate?
Is medication transported in a medicines trolley, and is this fit for purpose?
Is medication to be destroyed or returned to the pharmacy recorded (including the reason for destruction) and checked by two people?
fields.hint: Note whether this is done weekly.

fields.label: Are medication returns stored in clearly identified tamper-proof containers in a lockable area, separate from medicines in use?
Is medication that needs refrigerating stored in a locked 'medication only' fridge, or a lockable container in an ordinary fridge?
Are the current, minimum and maximum fridge temperatures, and the temperature of the main medication storage area, recorded on a monitoring chart every 24 hours?
Is action taken if temperatures are outside the recommended range (2–8°C for the fridge, below 25°C for the room)?
Is medication received with a MAR chart and checked / recorded by two people when it arrives at the home?
Are MAR charts completed fully, with no missing signatures, no out-of-stocks, correct codes, and time-specific medication given and recorded appropriately?
Do you have PRN protocols in place for residents?
When carers administer topical creams, thickeners, nutritional supplements and similar, do they complete the relevant paperwork?
Can you evidence best interest decisions and capacity assessments, signed by the relevant professional, for people who need medication given covertly?
For people receiving medication covertly, is information available to staff on how to administer it?
Is homely medication prescribed and administered as per the agreed organisational policy?
Can you evidence that medication reviews take place?
Do you have a policy on people self-medicating?
For those who self-medicate, can you provide evidence of risk assessments and regular reviews?
Do service users have a one-page profile on file in relation to their medication?
Is medication only administered by fully trained, competent carers?
Evidence and actions
fields.hint: What evidence you hold for medicines and clinical care, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: Are you aware of the Dignity in Care campaign, and can you evidence how the organisation delivers the 10 Dignity Do's (or an alternative)?
Do you review your staff on a regular basis to ensure a non-judgemental culture within the home?
Can you evidence that all people are treated as individuals, considering any relevant protected characteristics?
Is there evidence that the service considers individual preferences, e.g. habits, culture, faith and wishes?
Can you provide evidence that all of the workforce are up to date with dignity in care training?
Do staff and management interact with people and engage them in conversation?
Evidence and actions
fields.hint: What evidence you hold for dignity and equality, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: Do you have an up-to-date infection control policy, reviewed in the last 12 months?
Have you actioned the recommendations made?
Does your service undertake deep cleans, and are these clearly identified separately from daily cleans?
Is there evidence of personal protective equipment (PPE)?
Is there evidence that PPE is being used appropriately and taken off at the correct time?
Have you had an infection control inspection within the last 12 months?
fields.hint: Note the date.

fields.label: Do you encourage and maintain a safe standard of general hygiene?
fields.hint: Note how standards are maintained.

fields.label: Do you have a needlestick injury advice notice on display?
Do you have a system in place for managing clinical and non-clinical waste disposal?
Do you have documentation showing that staff have received or declined relevant vaccines?
Do service users receive support and training to enable them to contribute effectively to their own life skills?
Do all staff have up-to-date infection control training, refreshed every 2 years by e-learning or face-to-face training?
Evidence and actions
fields.hint: What evidence you hold for infection control, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: Do you offer and encourage a choice of menu / meals that promotes a healthy diet?
Are drinks and snacks available throughout the day and night?
Are fluid and nutrition charts put in place for residents where required?
Do residents' care plans reflect weight monitoring, and does this link into their risk assessment?
Do you have adapted cutlery and crockery available for those who need it?
Do the menus / meals meet each person's dietary and cultural needs, and do you review how well they work?
Do you provide a choice of dining experience, e.g. dining table / room, staggered dining times?
Do you promote malnutrition care planning in line with local care home guidance?
Do you have a process for identifying issues with nutrition?
Do you provide menus / nutritional information in accessible formats?
Do you ensure your staff are trained in meeting the cultural nutritional needs of the people they support?

fields.hint: What evidence you hold for nutrition, and any actions needed (what, who, by when)

fields.label: Do you have an activity coordinator within the home?
Does the activity coordinator engage all residents in activities to improve their physical and mental wellbeing?
Do you have examples of varied activity rotas that are outcome-based, built on residents' interests and recorded in the care plan?
Are the planned activities inclusive of residents who are frail, or who choose to remain in their room and are at risk of isolation?

fields.label: Does the coordinator include activities as part of the daily routine, and can this be evidenced in the care plan?
Do you have links to local faith groups?
Do you have community links / volunteers?

Can you evidence a variety of outcome-based and meaningful activity is available for all individuals?
Does the outdoor space enable individuals to take part in activities that promote positive outcomes?

Is there a feedback procedure on display and accessible to residents and relatives, including details of the CQC, local authority, Ombudsman and provider?
Do you give people, their families or representatives an opportunity to feed back on the service you provide?

Can you evidence that people get information and advice in formats tailored to their individual needs?

Do you have business contingency plans in place in the event of an emergency, are all staff aware of them, and do you have a managerial succession plan?
Do you have evidence that water temperatures are regularly taken and recorded, including bath / shower temperatures before a person is helped with personal care?
Are all fire exits clear, with signage displayed around the home?
Is there evidence that TMVs (thermostatic mixing valves) are being checked and serviced?

Is all tall furniture, such as wardrobes, secured to the walls in the home and residents' rooms?
Can you provide evidence of the most up-to-date electrical installation certificate (every 5 years)?
Can you provide evidence of the most up-to-date gas safety certificate (annually)?
Can you evidence measures are in place to protect people at risk of falling or climbing out of windows?
Are there agreed standards for the maintenance of residents' rooms, and are audits in place?
Do you have a process for equipment which is out of date or unsafe?
Is the equipment check completed by a competent person?
